settings.title: Settings

general.storage: API keys are stored in the operating system keychain. Sessions, costs and settings live in a local SQLite database in pumr's app data folder.

sandbox.title: Sandbox for commands
sandbox.hint: The operating system confines every command the agent runs, and whatever that command starts. It is a second layer behind the permission rules, for a command they misjudge. A command the sandbox stops can ask to run outside it; you are asked each time.
sandbox.unavailable: This system has no sandbox pumr can use, so commands run unconfined. It needs macOS, or Linux 5.19 or newer with Landlock.
sandbox.networkUnavailable: Closing the network is only possible on macOS.
sandbox.inlineCode: Run inline code in a tighter sandbox instead of asking
sandbox.inlineCodeHint: Inline node or python code, and scripts passed to them in a heredoc, cannot be checked like a command. While “All commands inside the project” is on, such code runs without a prompt in a tighter sandbox: it reaches only this computer, writes only to the project, your extra folders and temp folders, and cannot start apps, reach other programs or change git hooks. The same applies to a command whose arguments are only known when it runs. Code that names files outside the project, sensitive files or other websites still asks. If the sandbox stops a script, the agent can ask you to run it normally. macOS only.

modeHints.off: Commands run as your user, held back only by the permission rules.
modeHints.files: Commands write only to the project, your extra folders, temp folders and the folders listed below. They cannot read the folders that hold keys. On macOS they cannot start other apps either: open only works as a command of its own, which the permission rules check.
modeHints.filesAndNetwork: The same, and commands reach only this computer, except commands whose hosts you allowed. Installing packages then asks to run outside the sandbox.

sandbox.writable: Folders commands may also write to
sandbox.writableHint: The caches of build tools. Without them a build fails on its first download. A path starts with / or ~.
sandbox.unreadableHint: Where keys and tokens live. git, ssh and the cloud tools keep the folders they work with, and a folder you released for commands stays open. pumr's own data folder, with your chats and settings, is closed to commands as well, whatever this list holds.
sandbox.excluded: Commands that run outside the sandbox
sandbox.excludedHint: For tools that bring a sandbox of their own and fail inside this one, such as browser tests. An entry names how the command line begins; with * it is a pattern for the whole line.

hooks.title: Hooks
hooks.hint: A hook is a command of yours that pumr runs at a fixed moment of the agent's work. The model does not decide whether it runs, so it cannot forget it. Hooks run as you wrote them, without permission prompts and outside the sandbox.
hooks.protocol: A hook gets the details as JSON on standard input (tool_name, tool_input, tool_response) and the file a call names as $PUMR_FILE. Exit code 0 lets the agent go on. Exit code 2 hands what the hook printed to the agent and, before a tool call, refuses the call.

events.turnEnd: When the agent wants to finish

hooks.toolsPlaceholder: Every tool, or names such as edit|write
hooks.filesPlaceholder: Every file, or patterns such as *.ts

memory.title: Memory
memory.hint: pumr can remember how you like to work, for example how you want a code review reported, and tells the agent in every chat and every project. Nothing is remembered without your yes.
memory.enabledHint: Off, the entries below are kept, but the agent is not sent them and nothing new is suggested.
memory.suggestionsHint: When one of your messages shows a lasting preference, pumr asks after the answer whether to remember it: at most once per chat and once a day, and less often each time you do not save one. Off, pumr still remembers what you ask it to.
memory.placeholder: For example: When reviewing code, ask me for every finding whether to fix or skip it.

sounds.permissionHint: Played when the agent needs your approval or asks a question.

hotkeys.title: Keyboard shortcuts
hotkeys.hint: Click a shortcut and press the new key combination; Escape cancels. Shortcuts that work while typing need a modifier or a special key such as Enter. Fixed shortcuts are listed for reference.
hotkeys.closeTabHint: Closes the currently active session tab.
hotkeys.newSessionHint: Creates a new session in the active project.
hotkeys.deleteSessionHint: Deletes the session highlighted in the sidebar.
hotkeys.terminalHint: Shows or hides the terminal below the chat or editor.
hotkeys.terminalNewTabHint: Opens another terminal while the terminal is focused.
hotkeys.terminalCloseTabHint: Closes the active terminal while the terminal is focused.
hotkeys.windowToggleHint: Global shortcut that brings pumr to the active screen. Enable it under Window.
hotkeys.fixedHint: Built-in shortcut that cannot be changed.
hotkeys.chatToggleModeHint: Goes back to the mode the session was in before planning.

window.title: Window summoning
window.hint: Summon pumr to the screen you are working on with a global shortcut, even when another app is focused. Press it again to hide or minimize.
window.enableHint: Registers a system-wide shortcut. Disabled by default so pumr never claims a key you did not choose.
window.hotkeyHint: Click and press the key combination. Function keys work without a modifier; on macOS you may need to hold Fn.
window.behaviourHint: What the shortcut does when the window is already in front.
window.fillScreenHint: Make the summoned window fill the active monitor instead of keeping its previous size.
window.shortcutError: The system-wide shortcut could not be registered, so it does not summon pumr. Another app is probably using this key combination: choose a different one and save again.
window.waylandHint: On Wayland, apps cannot register system-wide shortcuts, so this shortcut does not work reliably here. Bind the command below to a key in your desktop's keyboard settings instead.
window.commandHint: Does what the shortcut does: summons pumr, or hides or minimizes it when it is in front. Bind it to a key in your desktop's keyboard settings.
window.commandActions: For a single action, end the command with one of these instead:
window.zoomHint: Scales the whole interface. Shortcut: Ctrl/⌘ + + to zoom in, Ctrl/⌘ + - to zoom out, Ctrl/⌘ + 0 to reset.

settings.autoCompactThreshold: Compact conversations at (% of context window)
settings.autoCompactThresholdHint: Once the context is this full, older messages are replaced by a summary for the model. 0 waits until the conversation no longer fits.
settings.autoCompactMaxTokensHint: Models lose track of a long context well before a large window is full. Also applies to models whose window size is unknown. 0 sets no limit.
settings.maxToolIterationsHint: How many consecutive tool calls the agent may make before it pauses and asks you to continue. The limit is a safety valve: it stops a model that gets stuck in a loop from running forever and burning tokens. 35 is a good default; raise it for long, multi-step tasks.
settings.autoContinueAllSessionsHint: When a session reaches the tool-call limit, keep going automatically instead of pausing. This removes the loop safety net, so a stuck agent may run until you stop it. You can also toggle this from the chat when a limit is reached.
settings.subagentModelHint: Model used for subagents. Leave empty to use the session's model.
settings.compactionModelHint: Model used to summarise long conversations. Leave empty to use the session's model.
settings.promptCachingHint: Mark the stable prompt prefix as cacheable so providers that support caching bill cached input tokens at a lower rate.
settings.verifyBeforeFinishHint: When the agent wants to finish after changing code without having run anything, it is asked once to run one of the project's checks (tests, build, lint). Costs at most one extra step per turn.
settings.mcpProgressiveDisclosureHint: When many MCP tools are connected, expose a tool_search/mcp_invoke pair instead of inlining every schema to save context. Small tool sets are always inlined.
settings.fileAccessRulesHint: Control which files the assistant may discover and read. User exemptions always win over every rule below.
settings.ignoreGitignoredHint: The assistant skips files that git ignores, such as build output, caches and local artifacts.
settings.scanGeneratedFiles: Allow scanning build files and dependencies
settings.scanGeneratedFilesHint: Exception to the .gitignore rule: also scan generated and dependency folders such as node_modules, dist, target, coverage or vendor, plus logs, caches and minified assets.
settings.ignoreLocalDatabasesHint: Skip local database files such as .sqlite, .db, .realm, .mdb or .accdb.
settings.ignoreEnvFilesHint: Skip .env files while keeping example, sample and template files readable.
settings.ignoreEnvFilesWarning: Warning: turning this off lets the assistant read .env files, which usually contain API keys, database passwords and access tokens. Only disable this if you trust the configured model and provider.
settings.fileIgnoreExemptionsHint: Glob patterns that the assistant may always read, even if covered by .gitignore, database or environment rules.
settings.advancedIgnoreHint: Fine-tune every built-in format. Entries follow their group switch above unless you override them here; your changes are remembered.
settings.commandRulesHint: Exact rules match command text literally; glob rules use wildcards. Both can coexist with the same text. Safety checks still apply.
settings.mcpToolGrantsHint: Tools of MCP servers that run without asking. An entry covers one tool of one server, whatever its arguments, and stops applying when that server's configuration changes. Use "allow always" in a permission prompt to create one.
settings.secretFoldersHint: Commands may use the sensitive files (keys, tokens, credentials) directly in these folders without asking. Folders below them are not included. Use "allow always" in a permission prompt to create one.
settings.noSecretFolders: No folders with released sensitive files yet.
settings.pathFoldersHint: Commands may put these folders on PATH without asking, although the assistant can change files in them. Use "allow always" in a permission prompt to add one.
settings.noPathFolders: No folders trusted on PATH yet.
settings.noCommandRules: No command rules yet. Use "allow always" in a permission prompt to create one.
settings.websiteRulesHint: Websites the assistant may visit, with its web tools or with commands such as curl, git and ssh. Deny rules win over allow rules; a plain domain also covers its subdomains. Use "allow always" or "deny always" in a permission prompt to create one.
settings.permissionPromptsHint: Choose what the main allow button does by default. Allow once approves a single request; allow for this session remembers folder access until the app restarts.
settings.autoApproveHint: Skip prompts for work the assistant can prove is safe. Dangerous commands, package downloads, websites that are not allowed yet, paths outside the project and sensitive files always ask.
settings.autoApproveReadOnlyHint: Allow inspection commands such as ls, grep and git status without asking.
settings.autoApprovePackageScriptsHint: Allow pnpm, npm, yarn, bun, ng, make and similar tools, and npx for tools the project already installed, when nothing points outside the project.
settings.autoApproveProjectExecutablesHint: Allow executables inside the project, such as ./node_modules/.bin/ng, without asking every time.
settings.autoApproveProjectCommandsHint: Allow any non-dangerous command whose paths stay inside the project, including inline node or python code that only reads. Dangerous commands, other inline code, package downloads, websites that are not allowed yet, sensitive files and anything outside still ask. The exception is inline node or python code that the sandbox runs instead of asking (see Sandbox).

permissionPreset.strictHint: Only read-only commands run without asking.
permissionPreset.balancedHint: Read-only commands, package managers, build runners and project executables run without asking.
permissionPreset.autonomousHint: Every non-dangerous command inside the project runs without asking.
permissionPreset.autonomousWarning: Autonomous trusts this project: its scripts, Makefiles and executables can do anything without a prompt, and inline code that only reads runs too. Other inline code, package downloads, websites that are not allowed yet, dangerous commands and anything outside the project still ask. The exception is inline node or python code that the sandbox runs instead of asking (see Sandbox).

permission.siteRuleHint: For example: docs.rs allows that site, *.github.com allows all its subdomains.
permission.siteRuleInvalid: This rule doesn't cover {{ host }} or is too broad, so {{ host }} will be saved instead.

scope.title: Rule scope
scope.hint: Choose how broadly this rule applies.

folderScope.hintRead: Opens the folder and everything below it for reading. Changes there still ask.

hostScope.title: Allow website
hostScope.hint: Adds the website and its subdomains to the allowed websites.

secretScope.title: Sensitive files
secretScope.hint: Commands may then use the keys, tokens and credential files directly in this folder without asking. Folders below it are not included.

pathScope.hint: A folder trusted on PATH may be put there by commands without asking. Its programs then run in place of others with the same name.

option.chat: Yes, and don't ask again in this chat for
option.session: Yes, and don't ask again until restart for

permission.keyboardHint: Press 1–{{ count }} or use ↑ ↓ and Enter · Esc denies
